name: Single sign-on (OIDC)
description: Single sign-on with any corporate OpenID Connect provider (Okta, Keycloak, Auth0, Entra ID…)

page.title: Single sign-on (OIDC)
page.description: Sign in with your company identity provider. Configure it in Settings › Modules.

steps: At the identity provider, create a "web" OpenID Connect application using the authorization code flow.
Register the callback URL above as a redirect URI.
Grant the openid, email and profile scopes and make sure the provider sends the email_verified = true claim.
Copy the Client ID and Client secret here and fill in the issuer or discovery URL.
Fill in the e-mail domains and, if you want, check "Require single sign-on".

button_label.label: Button label
button_label.help: Text shown on the login screen button

client_id.label: Client ID
client_id.help: Identifier of the application registered at the provider

client_secret.label: Client secret
client_secret.help: Application secret; stored encrypted and never shown again

domains.label: E-mail domains
domains.help: Domains that sign in through single sign-on, separated by commas (e.g. company.com). Empty = the button does not show on the login screen

require_sso.label: Require single sign-on
require_sso.help: Refuses password login for e-mails of these domains

shared.callbackHelp: Register exactly this address at the provider. The same URL is used for sign-in and for the calendar connection.
shared.statusUnavailable: The status could not be loaded right now.

login.title: Single sign-on
login.description: Users whose e-mail belongs to the domains below see the "{{label}}" button on the login screen. The account must already exist in Aphel and be a member of this organization.
login.required: Password login blocked for these domains
login.noDomains: No domain configured: the button does not show on the login screen.

calendar.title: {{provider}} calendar
calendar.description: Your CRM meetings go to your {{provider}} calendar and calendar events with CRM people become meetings here. When both sides change, the latest change wins.
calendar.notConfigured: An administrator must configure the module Client ID and Client secret before calendars can be connected.
calendar.noPermission: You are not allowed to connect the calendar.
calendar.syncQueued: Synchronization started; events show up in a few moments.
calendar.connectedToast: Calendar connected. The first synchronization has started.
calendar.confirmDescription: The stored access is deleted and synchronization stops. Meetings already in the CRM and in the calendar stay where they are.

calendarErrors.generic: The calendar could not be synchronized.
calendarErrors.access_denied: The authorization was canceled at the provider.
calendarErrors.permission_denied: You are not allowed to connect the calendar.
calendarErrors.calendar_no_refresh_token: The provider did not grant offline access. Connect again and accept every permission.
calendarErrors.calendar_authorization_revoked: The calendar access was revoked or expired. Reconnect the calendar.
calendarErrors.calendar_member_unavailable: The user is no longer an active member of the organization.
calendarErrors.calendar_permission_revoked: The permission to sync the calendar was removed from this user.
calendarErrors.calendar_meeting_type_not_found: The activity type configured for meetings does not exist or is inactive.
calendarErrors.calendar_api_failed: The provider refused the calendar operation.
calendarErrors.sso_not_configured: The module is not configured yet.
calendarErrors.sso_disabled: The module is disabled in this organization.
calendarErrors.invalid_state: The connection request expired. Try again.
calendarErrors.token_exchange_failed: The provider refused the authorization. Check the Client ID, the secret and the callback URL.
calendarErrors.invalid_token: The provider returned an invalid identity.
calendarErrors.provider_unavailable: The provider did not answer. Try again in a moment.
